Path ["map",0] returns the identical array, while ["map",0,1] returns "three" complete true. Thus a two-entry map appears to omit 2000 entries at its own collection level.
runtime/mcp-views.mo:570-584 initializes value to item.value and appends it unchanged when a map key is incomplete; only the complete-key branch wraps it in Json.Array([value, second.value]).
runtime/mcp-views.mo:scalar cuts Text with cut(size, budget), where size is the byte length; walk then excludes that current entry from its omitted = count - i - 1 map-entry count.
docs/design/introspection.md section 3.3 specifies Map as an array of [key, value] pairs, while the authenticated-live-views amendment distinguishes omitted collection counts from text/byte counts.
runtime/mcp-views.mo:saved_state's pair branch already returns Json.Array([key.value, value.value]) and substitutes cut(1, key.left) when the key is incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: In walk's map branch, always produce the pair wrapper. If item.complete is false, use a value-side cut marker without attempting to read item.next, matching saved_state's selected-pair handling; alternatively emit one collection marker for count - i remaining entries. Add an oversized-key map regression alongside the existing map-path HTTP checks.
findings.title: Preserve map entry shape when a key truncates
findings.why_it_matters: Inspecting a map with a key that exceeds the rendering budget emits its byte-count truncation marker directly into the map array, where the documented representation reserves objects of that shape for omitted collection elements. An operator cannot distinguish omitted map entries from a partially rendered key and loses the promised [key, value] entry structure. Preserve the pair wrapper when its key is cut, as the existing selected-pair path already does, or omit the entire entry with an accurate remaining-entry count.
findings.validation_reason: For a saved map whose key exceeds the remaining rendering budget, new runtime/mcp-views.mo:474 returns a byte-count cut marker and lines 570-592 append it directly instead of a [key, value] pair, violating docs/design/introspection.md:139 and 749-751; the operator dispatch at line 202 reaches this renderer without a key-size guard, although incidence was not measured under the read-only review constraints.

docs/design/introspection.md: Authenticated live views requires recovery and successful append to populate metadata, successful snapshot to clear it, failed append to leave it unchanged, and successful append followed by failed snapshot to retain the committed entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend memory_store to compare log entries before and after reopening, including handler, arrival and argument_bytes. Extend uncertain_commit to assert refused appends preserve metadata and reopened committed appends appear; extend failed_snapshot to assert entry 100 remains before reopening and the successful recovery snapshot clears the log.
findings.title: Assert recovered and failed-write log metadata
findings.why_it_matters: A service can restart with correct application state but an empty or incorrect mo-log, and the current tests would still pass. The only new log-entry assertions inspect successful live commits; existing reopen, uncertain-append and failed-snapshot tests check state and durable sequence without checking the newly maintained metadata. Those paths determine whether operators see the committed tail and whether a failed snapshot incorrectly hides it.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added recovery/append/snapshot metadata transitions in src/vm/service.c have no assertions after the reachable reopen, refused-append and failed-snapshot triggers already exercised in tests/test_service_store.c:435-501: all log accessor assertions are confined to live successful commits at lines 324-327, and ci/check_operator.py:113-116 checks only an initial timer entry; this confirms the stated coverage gap, not an observed metadata malfunction.

evidence: tests/runtime/mcp-rpc-check.mo:247 --   tight = Mcp.prepare(descriptor, key, 2048) or stop "bounded catalog"
tests/runtime/mcp-rpc-check.mo:275 --   require(Mcp.prepare(descriptor, key, 100) == None)

The supplied diff deletes the expected-envelope bound calculation, prepare(bound - 1) rejection, and exact page equality assertion. runtime/mcp.mo:prepare checks every single-entry page against response_bytes; its page_size arithmetic remains sensitive to exact equality.
findings.first_evidence: tests/runtime/mcp-rpc-check.mo:247 --   tight = Mcp.prepare(descriptor, key, 2048) or stop "bounded catalog"
findings.suggested_fix: Build the expected one-tool JSON-RPC envelopes with the maximum-length escaped ID and the appropriate nextCursor for each catalog entry; take their maximum serialized byte count. Assert Mcp.prepare succeeds at that bound and fails at bound - 1, and assert the maximal entry's page matches its expected envelope.
findings.title: Restore exact catalog byte-boundary coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The replacement test no longer detects an off-by-one refusal of a catalog that exactly fits its response budget. It accepts 2048 bytes and refuses 100 bytes, whereas the deleted test pinned acceptance at the exact serialized size and rejection one byte below it. Operator entries change the largest required page, so retain the new traversal test and derive the new exact minimum independently from serialized one-tool envelopes.
findings.validation_reason: The reviewed diff removes the serialized-envelope exact-bound acceptance, bound-minus-one refusal and page-equality assertions from tests/runtime/mcp-rpc-check.mo, replacing them with 2048-byte acceptance and 100-byte refusal at lines 247 and 275; an exactly fitting single-entry page remains a reachable boundary in runtime/mcp.mo:45-51 and 78-93, so the stated regression in boundary coverage is established without asserting an existing runtime off-by-one defect.

testing_gaps: The new saved-state renderer manually decodes IEEE-754 values, but ci/check_operator.py exercises only 1.5 and tests/runtime/mcp-views-check.mo exercises only Int. Add deterministic rendering checks for negative zero, minimum subnormal, maximum finite, NaN and both infinities to pin the promised Float representation independently of the crash-only fuzz oracle.
